literal: your own spear against your own shield
source: 《韩非子·难一》 (public domain), retold in our own words.
story: Ancient China, state of Chu, about 2,300 years ago. In a busy market, a loud seller shows off his goods. He holds up a huge shield: 'My shield is so strong that nothing can pierce it!' Then he holds up a spear: 'My spear is so sharp that it pierces anything!' The crowd is impressed, until an old man asks: 'So what happens if your spear hits your shield?' The seller freezes, holding the spear in one hand and the shield in the other, and has no answer.
continuity: - WANG, the seller: loud, chubby man about 40, round red face, big grin, thin black mustache, black hair in a bun tied with a yellow cloth, ochre-yellow robe with rolled-up sleeves, brown apron.
- THE OLD MAN: thin old man about 70, long white beard, bald on top with white hair at the sides, slate-blue robe, wooden walking stick.

- THE SHIELD AND THE SPEAR: one huge round wooden shield painted dark red with a round bronze boss in the middle (no symbols, no writing); one long spear with a shiny bronze tip and a red tassel. His stall: a wooden table with more spears and shields leaning on it (no signs, no writing).
- SETTING: a busy ancient town market: packed-earth street, wooden stalls with plain cloth awnings (no signs, no writing), soft daylight.
scenes: The twist (used as the hook, first frame of the video)

Medium shot, both faces clear. Wang stands frozen at his stall, the spear in one hand and the shield in the other, eyes wide, sweat drops flying, mouth open with no words. In front of him the Old Man leans on his stick and points calmly from the spear to the shield, one eyebrow raised. This is the most important image; the editor will push in on it.

Wide shot of the busy market. Wang stands behind his wooden stall full of spears and shields, one hand cupped at his mouth, shouting to the street with a huge grin. (Only Wang in the foreground; a few small, blurred shoppers far in the background are fine.)
Wang holds the huge red shield up high in front of him and knocks on it proudly with his fist, chest puffed out, very pleased with himself. (Only Wang.)
Wang thrusts the spear up dramatically, the bronze tip gleaming with a little sparkle, a confident, dramatic pose like a hero. (Only Wang.)

A small crowd of three or four shoppers in plain robes gathers in front of the stall, nodding and gasping, impressed. Wang beams at them, holding the spear and shield. The Old Man stands at the back of the crowd, stroking his beard thoughtfully.
The Old Man steps forward from the crowd and raises one finger, calm and polite, with a small sly smile. Wang leans toward him, still grinning, expecting a customer.

Close-up, comic: the Old Man gently taps the tip of Wang's spear against the middle of Wang's own shield with his walking stick, looking up at Wang with raised eyebrows. Wang's face goes pale and stiff, a single sweat drop rolling down.
The spear and shield (background for the big title)

The red shield lying flat on the packed-earth ground in the lower half of the frame, with the spear lying across it. The upper half is a calm, plain sky-and-awning background with soft grey ink washes and almost nothing in it (we place the big title there). No people.

The same WANG (round red face, thin mustache, hair bun with a yellow cloth) in a modern ochre hoodie sits at a café table proudly holding up a green salad bowl in one hand, while his other hand holds a fork stuck in a huge slice of chocolate cake. Beside him the same OLD MAN (long white beard, bald on top) in a slate-blue cardigan raises one eyebrow. No text, no logos, no menus with writing.
lines: One simple question, and he had no answer.
A man at the market sold shields and spears.
This shield? Nothing can break it!
And this spear? It breaks through anything!
Then an old man asked one question.
What if your spear hits your shield?
Your own spear against your own shield.
Like saying you're on a diet… over a second dessert.
title: His spear beats any shield… and his shield stops any spear 🛡️ | 自相矛盾
desc: 自相矛盾 (zì xiāng máo dùn) = contradicting yourself. Ever done that? 👇
pinned: 自 self · 相 each other · 矛 spear · 盾 shield. 📝 他说要减肥，又点了两份甜点，真是自相矛盾。(Tā shuō yào jiǎnféi, yòu diǎn le liǎng fèn tiándiǎn, zhēn shì zì xiāng máo dùn.) = He says he's on a diet, then orders two desserts. That's contradicting yourself.
